sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page yeme1237 (Yemeni Sign Language; Sign Language > Arab Sign family) and reference record 460304.
sources.note: Zero descriptive references. References cited: Hendriks & Zeshan 2009 (pp. 223-224, lexicostatistics), Al-Fityani & Padden 2010 (lexicostatistics), Al-Muslat 1994 (pp. 279-280, teacher recruitment), Wittmann 1991 (classification), Jaza 2015 (pp. 570-571, Kurdish vs Iraqi SL). None is a grammar, phonology or sketch.
Stub: Arab sign-language family, no ISO 639-3 code; 'It is not clear how close are the sign languages of the two former Yemeni states'; sole reference is Hendriks 2008; nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Mohammed, R.A.A., M.A.A. Mosleh, A.A.A. Mohammed & E. Esmail. 2025. ArYSL: Arabic Yemeni sign language dataset. Data in Brief 61: 111996. doi:10.1016/j.dib.2025.111996 (PMC12433467).
sources.note: Nothing. Computer-vision image dataset of 32 isolated static signs; no linguistic description. States the classes 'follow semantic definitions established in the Unified Yemeni Sign Language Dictionary' but gives no citation for that dictionary; its 8 references are all CV/dataset papers.

sources.citation: Hendriks, Bernadet. 2008. Jordanian Sign Language: aspects of grammar from a cross-linguistic perspective. Utrecht: LOT (LOT dissertation series 193).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on Yemeni Sign Language stress or phonology. Yemeni SL appears only in the lexicostatistical survey (sec. 2.3, pp. 27-36): three wordlists from Sana'a, Aden and al-Mukalla, 64-67% similar to each other, forties/high thirties vs Jordan/Syria/Iraq; 'Egypt and Yemen have somewhat higher similarity scores, possibly because in Yemen many teachers in schools for the Deaf are Egyptian' (p. 35). The book's own prosody remarks concern Jordanian SL (LIU) only.
